subtype: Approach: using helplines and emergency services when danger is immediate [Action]
passage: I'm Bhupen, and I live above the stationery shop, so I see most of what happens on our lane. Tuesday evening Vikas came out of the gully with his phone against his ear, walking so fast he nearly hit my cycle. He was saying, "Papa, come now, it's Ashwin, my best friend, he says he doesn't want to be here anymore, he's at his flat." Then he put his father on hold and dialled the emergency number. He gave the flat number and the building name twice, slowly. He did not run off to Ashwin's himself. When his father's scooter turned in, Vikas pointed and they left together. I couldn't tell whether he was frightened or just sure of what to do. His hands were shaking, but his voice was not. Later his father told me Ashwin was safe and his parents were with him.

qa.q: What did Vikas do after he put his father on hold?
qa.a: He dialled the emergency number and gave the flat number and the building name twice, slowly.

qa.q: How can you tell that Vikas was frightened but steady, and how sure can Bhupen be?
qa.a: His hands were shaking but his voice was not, so he seemed scared yet sure of what to do, though Bhupen admits not being able to tell for certain.

qa.q: If Vikas could not reach his father, what else could he do, and why?
qa.a: He could call a mental health helpline or another adult nearby along with the emergency number, because immediate danger needs adults and trained responders, not a teen alone.

qa.q: How might Ashwin see Vikas's quick calls later?
qa.a: Ashwin may feel frightened or embarrassed, yet also cared for, since a friend acted at once and adults reached him.

grounding: A teen calls a family adult and the emergency number at once when a friend is in immediate danger, seen through a bystander's eyes.
